title: Cooking Cheat
paragraphs: It’s taking quite a long time to get through the mountain pass. By the way, during activation periods, the atmospheric flow worsens, making it difficult to travel to activation sites by air. We’re staying at a rest stop along the way for the night and should arrive by tomorrow morning.
“Hey, Raphtalia-chan.”
This happened just as I was about to sit down and have a meal with the slaves. Father called out to Big Sister.
“What is it?”
“Well… I’ve been meaning to say this for a while now, and everyone’s been considerate enough to keep quiet about it, but…”
With Father’s words, Ren, Itsuki, and almost everyone there turned their attention to him.
“You don’t have to force yourself to smile, okay?” Father spoke to her with concern.
However, Big Sister once again put on that pasted-on smile.
“I-I’m fine! Right, everyone?”
“Raphtalia-chan…”
Her friend looked at her with concern, watching as she glanced around with that forced smile. Indeed. I had been a little worried as well.
“What’s wrong? Hey, everyone?”
“B-Buu…”
“W-Well, I say…”

Everyone avoided her gaze, responding with unease. This feels familiar. Before I was summoned… back in middle school or high school, when I was chasing after pigs and one of them ran into a wall, the atmosphere felt just like this.

“Everyone told me about their experiences as slaves and the suffering they endured during the Waves today. I know I can only imagine what it was like, and I may not have the right to say anything… but I can at least listen if you need to talk.”
Ren and Itsuki both seemed to be showing a cooperative stance on this. They had been chatting casually with the slaves, acting as conversation partners.
“We’ve thought things through enough to challenge the Waves to prevent more tragedies.”
“After hearing their stories… and seeing all of you covered in wounds, it really made me realize that this isn’t a game. Of course, the biggest reason is what’s happened over the past few days.”

Ren and Itsuki must have had a lot on their minds as well. In a way, it feels like they’ve steeled their resolve faster than last time. I remember that it took them a bit longer to shed the game-like mentality before. But through their interactions with the slaves, they seem to have snapped out of it rather quickly this time. This is quite the discovery. It’s probably because they witnessed the harsh realities the slaves endured firsthand.
“Y-You’re all worrying too much… I’m really fine…”
“…That’s not how it looks at all.”

Father locked eyes with her and stared seriously. Big Sister, looking uncomfortable, glanced at her friend and Keel with that same pasted-on smile. Then, Father gently hugged her and stroked her head softly.
“Raphtalia-chan. I won’t force you. But… if you’re sad, it’s okay to cry, you know? When I see you forcing yourself to smile… I can’t help but worry.”
Her friend also placed a hand on her shoulder, following Father’s lead.
“The people of the country are doing their best to help rebuild the village, and we’re helping too. So… don’t carry everything alone. Rely on us.”
“I-I’m really fine…”
Father looked into her eyes. Was this an attempt to persuade her?
“The world is full of cruel people. I understand that you might not trust me. We’ve only known each other for a few days. But… it’s okay to rely on the village kids, isn’t it?”
“Bubu, bubububu!”
At that moment, Keel spoke up with determination. Surely, this would turn the conversation in a positive direction. Keel is quite reliable.
“Yeah. Raphtalia-chan, we all feel the same.”
When her friends said that, Big Sister fell silent, as if deep in thought. Sensing that any further persuasion might be pointless, Father and the others, though still worried, stood up.
“Well then, everyone, shall we go get something to eat?”

With that, we all headed to the dining hall adjacent to the inn at the rest stop. While other guests were already eating, we were guided to a table as a group. Father glanced at the food being served to the other customers.
There weren’t many diners around. In fact, the tavern seemed much livelier and noisier. It looked like adventurers had gathered there.
“Um…”
“Ah, yes! What would you like to order?”
Father called out to the server to ask about the menu that everyone might want. But since most of the slaves weren’t very literate, they couldn’t quite imagine what the menu offered.
“I know it’s a lot to ask, but could I borrow part of the kitchen? I’d like to cook something.”
“Huh?”
Oh? Is Father planning to do something? The server looked confused.
“Please. I’m asking to borrow the kitchen to prepare a dish using these ingredients.”
“Ah, understood.”
Fiancée handed the server some money, who then went to consult with the owner. After a short while, the server returned.
“Fortunately, no other customers are using the kitchen tonight, so you’re welcome to use it. This way, please.”
“Thank you.”
Father bowed and followed the staff member to the kitchen.
“Ah, I’ll help.”

Big sister stood up and followed as well. Hmm, helping Father, that’s quite commendable. Just like in the first world… Oh? Now that I think about it, I’ve never seen her helping Father with cooking before, have I? Well, perhaps I just haven’t noticed.
“Thanks. I’d appreciate the help.”
Soon, the sounds of cooking began to echo from the kitchen. This promises to be a delightful dinner tonight.
“Wasn’t Naofumi-san really good at cooking, according to Motoyasu-san?”
“He explained that weirdly in detail on the first day of the summoning, didn’t he?”
“Maybe he’s preparing a comforting meal for all the former slaves?”
“Probably. He seems to care a lot about them.”
Ah, this is Father’s way of showing kindness. …But why is the cook sitting at one of the tables, looking pale?
“Is he speechless in a good way? Or did he get sick from some bizarre dish and run away? Which do you think it is?”
“If we trust what Motoyasu-san said, I’d say it’s the former…”
Ren and Itsuki were glued to that sight. As we talked, the server, still looking dazed, soon brought in the food. What was served… was a children’s meal.
Chicken rice with a little flag stuck in it, accompanied by a hamburger and pasta. The flag seemed to be crafted from a wooden skewer. I could tell that Keel and the other slaves were excited.
Now that I think about it, during our free time in the first world, I did talk to Father about children’s meals. The slaves really liked that kind of food. He remembered what I told him!
“Alright, it’s ready. Everyone, go ahead and eat. I’ll keep making more.”
Father peeked out from the kitchen and told everyone to start eating. And then, more and more dishes were brought out for us.
“Oh? This is the dish we had on the first day. Whoa, this is right up our alley… I mean, it tastes like it’s made for Japanese people.”
“Yeah, it seems Motoyasu-san’s story was true. But unlike us, their dishes seem to have a Melromarc-style flavor.”
“So this is the so-called cooking cheat… Adjusting the taste to match the homeland of the person eating…”

Ren and Itsuki started devouring the food that had been served. Of course, I was eating too. Then, all of a sudden, the cook who had been looking pale stood up with a clatter and ran toward the kitchen. Is everything okay?

I followed after him to make sure Father wasn’t in danger. If he dared to attack Father, I’d kill him. But as it turned out, the cook seemed to be competing with Father, trying to match his cooking. His eyes were glued to Father’s movements.
“Uh… I’m really not that great at cooking, you know…”

Isn’t this turning into an unspoken cooking showdown between Father and the cook? Father had assumed that the cuisine of this world was just unfamiliar. With all this going on, we thoroughly enjoyed the dishes that were served.
